title: Ice cream innovation
paragraphs: Is there anything nicer than a cooling ice cream on a hot summer's day? This traditional treat is centuries old, but our tastes and consumer habits are evolving. How is the ice cream production process changing, and who is driving this change?

Making ice cream is a time-consuming process. While the recipe is simple – milk, sugar and fat, plus flavours and colours – ice cream has a complex chemistry. Getting the balance right between ice, fat and air is important if the ice cream is to have the right texture. To achieve this, the ingredients need to be mixed and heated, then cooled and frozen – a process that takes time and uses a lot of energy. Designers and engineers are working to improve the production process with new specialised equipment to make it increasingly automated. For now, however, even with the help of robots and 3D printers, it can take up to two years from testing a new frozen dessert product to it being available to consumers.

And demand is only going up. According to the food packaging company Tetra Pak, more than 25 billion litres of ice cream were eaten worldwide in 2021. While the US and China are the biggest consumers, data from NielsenIQ shows that people in the UK bought 28% more ice cream during the UK's record-breaking summer compared to a year earlier. Clearly, rising temperatures can explain why some people are buying more ice cream, but it's not the only explanation. The pandemic has seen people reaching for pleasures they can enjoy at home, which include eating indulgent foods. And worries about the cost-of-living crisis could have a similar effect, as even a premium ice cream is an affordable treat.

So, what new things can we expect on a stick or in a cone? Consumers of all ages buy ice cream, but it is millennial consumers who are driving interest in more original flavours, including spices. Dairy still dominates, but plant-based ice cream, sorbets and low-calorie choices are a growing part of the frozen dessert market. But, according to Elsebeth Baungaard, portfolio manager at Tetra Pak, the next global trend will be less about innovation and more about portion size. "I'm sorry to say it's simply shrinking", she says. "But the quality will be higher."

vocabulary.entry: evolve /ɪˈvɒlv/ v. 演变；发展；进化

vocabulary.translation: 语言会随着时间不断发展演变。

vocabulary.entry: consumer habit /kənˈsjuːmə ˈhæbɪt/ n. 消费习惯
vocabulary.example: Advertising can shape and change people's consumer habits.
vocabulary.translation: 广告能够塑造并改变人们的消费习惯。

vocabulary.entry: production process /prəˈdʌkʃn ˈprəʊses/ n. 生产过程；制作工艺

vocabulary.translation: 这家工厂正在升级生产工艺以减少浪费。

vocabulary.entry: time-consuming /ˌtaɪm kənˈsjuːmɪŋ/ adj. 耗时的；费时间的

vocabulary.translation: 手动做这项研究十分耗时。

vocabulary.translation: 这种面料的化学性质使其具有防水性。

vocabulary.example: The cake has a light and fluffy texture.
vocabulary.translation: 这款蛋糕口感松软轻盈。

vocabulary.entry: ingredient /ɪnˈɡriːdiənt/ n. （食物的）原料；成分

vocabulary.entry: specialised equipment /ˈspeʃəlaɪzd ɪˈkwɪpmənt/ n. 专用设备；专业器材
vocabulary.example: The lab is equipped with specialised equipment for chemical analysis.
vocabulary.translation: 这个实验室配备了用于化学分析的专用设备。

vocabulary.entry: automated /ˈɔːtəmeɪtɪd/ adj. 自动化的；自动操作的
vocabulary.example: The company has an automated assembly line for car parts.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司有一条汽车零部件自动化生产线。

vocabulary.entry: increasingly /ɪnˈkriːsɪŋli/ adv. 越来越多地；日益
vocabulary.example: People are increasingly concerned about environmental protection.
vocabulary.translation: 人们越来越关注环境保护。

vocabulary.entry: frozen dessert /ˈfrəʊzn dɪˈzɜːt/ n. 冷冻甜品
vocabulary.example: The shop has a wide selection of frozen desserts for summer.
vocabulary.translation: 这家店夏天有各式各样的冷冻甜品可供选择。

vocabulary.entry: worldwide /ˌwɜːldˈwaɪd/ adv. 遍及全球地；在世界范围内
vocabulary.example: This brand of chocolate is sold worldwide.
vocabulary.translation: 这个品牌的巧克力在全球销售。

vocabulary.entry: record-breaking /ˌrekɔːd ˈbreɪkɪŋ/ adj. 破纪录的；创纪录的
vocabulary.example: The area had a record-breaking heatwave last July.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区去年七月遭遇了创纪录的热浪。

vocabulary.entry: pandemic /pænˈdemɪk/ n. （全球性）流行病；大流行病
vocabulary.example: The pandemic has had a huge impact on the global economy.
vocabulary.translation: 这场大流行病对全球经济造成了巨大影响。

vocabulary.entry: reach for /riːtʃ fɔː(r)/ 伸手去拿；寻求（精神上的）慰藉
vocabulary.example: When she's sad, she reaches for a book to distract herself.
vocabulary.translation: 她难过时，会拿起一本书来分散注意力。

vocabulary.entry: indulgent /ɪnˈdʌldʒənt/ adj. （食物）奢华的；享受型的；放纵的

vocabulary.translation: 我会在生日时犒劳自己吃一顿丰盛的大餐。

vocabulary.example: Many people are cutting back on spending due to the cost-of-living crisis.
vocabulary.translation: 受生活成本危机影响，很多人都在削减开支。

vocabulary.entry: premium /ˈpriːmiəm/ adj. 优质的；高端的 n. 溢价

vocabulary.translation: 我们售卖从印度进口的高端茶叶。

vocabulary.entry: affordable /əˈfɔːdəbl/ adj. 买得起的；价格实惠的
vocabulary.example: The hotel offers affordable rooms for budget travellers.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店为经济型游客提供价格实惠的房间。

vocabulary.entry: stick /stɪk/ n. 棒；棍（食品专用，冰棒/棒棒糖的棍）
vocabulary.example: The child was licking a strawberry ice cream on a stick.
vocabulary.translation: 那个孩子正舔着一支草莓冰棒。

vocabulary.entry: cone /kəʊn/ n. （冰淇淋的）锥形蛋筒；甜筒
vocabulary.example: I ordered a chocolate ice cream in a sugar cone.
vocabulary.translation: 我点了一个装在甜蛋筒里的巧克力冰淇淋。

vocabulary.entry: millennial /mɪˈleniəl/ adj. 千禧一代的 n. 千禧一代
vocabulary.example: Millennial consumers value experience more than material things.
vocabulary.translation: 千禧一代消费者更看重体验而非物质东西。

vocabulary.entry: original flavour /əˈrɪdʒənl ˈfleɪvə(r)/ n. 独创口味；特色风味
vocabulary.example: The brand launched four new original flavours of ice cream this year.
vocabulary.translation: 这个品牌今年推出了四款冰淇淋新独创口味。

vocabulary.entry: spice /spaɪs/ n. 香料；调味品 v. 加香料于
vocabulary.example: We use a variety of spices in our curries.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在咖喱里加了多种香料。

vocabulary.entry: dominate /ˈdɒmɪneɪt/ v. 主导；占优势；支配
vocabulary.example: Large corporations dominate the global soft drink market.
vocabulary.translation: 大型企业主导着全球软饮市场。

vocabulary.entry: sorbet /ˈsɔːbeɪ/ n. 雪葩；果汁冰糕
vocabulary.example: Lemon sorbet is a refreshing choice after a heavy meal.
vocabulary.translation: 吃完大餐后，柠檬雪葩是清爽的选择。

vocabulary.entry: low-calorie /ˌləʊ ˈkæləri/ adj. 低热量的
vocabulary.example: This low-calorie drink is popular with people on a diet.
vocabulary.translation: 这款低热量饮品很受节食人士的欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: portfolio manager /pɔːtˈfəʊliəʊ ˈmænɪdʒə(r)/ n. 产品组合经理
vocabulary.example: The portfolio manager is responsible for developing new product lines.
vocabulary.translation: 产品组合经理负责开发新的产品线。

vocabulary.entry: innovation /ˌɪnəˈveɪʃn/ n. 创新；革新；新事物
vocabulary.example: The company is known for its innovation in mobile technology.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司以其在移动技术领域的创新而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: portion size /ˈpɔːʃn saɪz/ n. （食物的）分量；份装大小
vocabulary.example: The restaurant has reduced the portion size of its steaks.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅缩小了牛排的分量。

vocabulary.entry: shrink /ʃrɪŋk/ v. （尺寸、分量）缩小；收缩；缩水
vocabulary.example: The portion size of the dessert has shrunk in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 这款甜品的分量近些年缩水了。

sentences.english: Is there anything nicer than a cooling ice cream on a hot summer's day?
sentences.chinese: 还有什么比在炎热夏日里来一份清凉的冰淇淋更惬意的事吗？

sentences.english: This traditional treat is centuries old, but our tastes and consumer habits are evolving.
sentences.chinese: 这种传统美食已有数百年历史，但我们的口味和消费习惯却在不断演变。

sentences.english: How is the ice cream production process changing, and who is driving this change?
sentences.chinese: 冰淇淋的生产流程正发生着怎样的变化？又是谁在推动这些变化呢？

sentences.english: Making ice cream is a time-consuming process.
sentences.chinese: 制作冰淇淋是一个耗时的过程。

sentences.english: While the recipe is simple – milk, sugar and fat, plus flavours and colours – ice cream has a complex chemistry.
sentences.chinese: 尽管配方很简单——牛奶、糖、脂肪，再加上调味剂和色素——但冰淇淋的制作却涉及复杂的化学变化。

sentences.english: Getting the balance right between ice, fat and air is important if the ice cream is to have the right texture.
sentences.chinese: 要让冰淇淋拥有恰到好处的口感，关键在于平衡好冰、脂肪和空气三者的比例。

sentences.english: To achieve this, the ingredients need to be mixed and heated, then cooled and frozen – a process that takes time and uses a lot of energy.
sentences.chinese: 为了达到这个效果，原料需要经过混合、加热，再冷却、冷冻，整个过程既耗时又耗能。

sentences.english: Designers and engineers are working to improve the production process with new specialised equipment to make it increasingly automated.
sentences.chinese: 设计师和工程师们正研发新型专业设备来改进生产流程，使其自动化程度越来越高。

sentences.english: For now, however, even with the help of robots and 3D printers, it can take up to two years from testing a new frozen dessert product to it being available to consumers.
sentences.chinese: 不过目前，即便有机器人和3D打印机的助力，一款新冷冻甜品从测试到面向消费者上市，也可能需要长达两年的时间。

sentences.english: And demand is only going up.
sentences.chinese: 冰淇淋的需求还在持续增长。

sentences.english: According to the food packaging company Tetra Pak, more than 25 billion litres of ice cream were eaten worldwide in 2021.
sentences.chinese: 据利乐食品包装公司的数据显示，2021年全球冰淇淋的消费量超过250亿升。

sentences.english: While the US and China are the biggest consumers, data from NielsenIQ shows that people in the UK bought 28% more ice cream during the UK's record-breaking summer compared to a year earlier.
sentences.chinese: 美国和中国是最大的消费市场，而尼尔森IQ的数据表明，在英国创纪录高温的那个夏天，人们购买的冰淇淋数量与去年同时期相比增长了28%。

sentences.english: Clearly, rising temperatures can explain why some people are buying more ice cream, but it's not the only explanation.
sentences.chinese: 显然，气温上升是冰淇淋销量增加的原因之一，但这并非唯一的因素。

sentences.english: The pandemic has seen people reaching for pleasures they can enjoy at home, which include eating indulgent foods.
sentences.chinese: 疫情期间，人们更倾向于寻求可以在家享受的乐趣，吃些解馋的美食便是其中之一。

sentences.english: And worries about the cost-of-living crisis could have a similar effect, as even a premium ice cream is an affordable treat.
sentences.chinese: 而对生活成本危机的担忧也可能产生类似的影响，因为即便是高端冰淇淋，也算得上是一种价格亲民的享受。

sentences.english: So, what new things can we expect on a stick or in a cone?
sentences.chinese: 那么，未来我们能在冰淇淋棒或蛋筒里吃到些什么新花样呢？

sentences.english: Consumers of all ages buy ice cream, but it is millennial consumers who are driving interest in more original flavours, including spices.
sentences.chinese: 各个年龄段的消费者都会购买冰淇淋，但正是千禧一代消费者推动了人们对更具创意的口味的兴趣，包括添加香料的冰淇淋。

sentences.english: Dairy still dominates, but plant-based ice cream, sorbets and low-calorie choices are a growing part of the frozen dessert market.
sentences.chinese: 乳制品冰淇淋仍占据主导地位，但植物基冰淇淋、果汁冰沙和低热量冰淇淋在冷冻甜品市场的占比正不断提升。

sentences.english: But, according to Elsebeth Baungaard, portfolio manager at Tetra Pak, the next global trend will be less about innovation and more about portion size.
sentences.chinese: 不过，利乐公司的投资组合经理埃尔斯贝思·邦高指出，下一个全球趋势将不再侧重于创新，而是聚焦分量。

sentences.english: "I'm sorry to say it's simply shrinking", she says. "But the quality will be higher."
sentences.chinese: “很遗憾地说，分量确实在变小，”她表示，“但品质会变得更高。”
